name: bg-stractium

frames.best_why: Frame 5 shows the full spiny form centred and evenly lit, with every shard visible.

tagline: A glossy orb erupts into layered metal fins and folds back again.
summary: A full-bleed animated 3D backdrop: a dark red and teal organic mass that continuously morphs between a smooth sphere and a burst of blade-like spines. The viewpoint drifts and follows the pointer.
appearance: A pale blue-white sky gradient fills the frame behind a large glossy form in dark red, teal and silver. In some frames it is a smooth sphere; in others it bursts into layered, feather-like fins and floating shards. White text reads Stractium over the middle.
behaviour: Runs unattended: the form slowly unfurls from a sphere into spiny blades and back. Moving the pointer shifts the camera angle, and the drifting viewpoint makes the shards catch the light.
use_when: A marketing hero or splash screen needs a moving 3D backdrop without shipping image assets.
avoid_when: A costly per-pixel ray march never idles, and its fixed pale sky fights dark themes and white text.
customise: Hue, saturation, brightness, speed, pointer sensitivity, damping and noise opacity/scale are props; the shader geometry itself needs a source edit.
weight_why: Ray-marches up to 250 steps per pixel every frame.

a11y.note: Decorative canvas with no ARIA role or reduced-motion check, and the animation never stops.

issues: The demo declares a black container, but the frames show a pale sky filling the stage.
The white Stractium label is nearly invisible against the bright background.
polish_why: Striking raymarched form with believable shading; the white demo label fades into the sky.
title: Stractium Background
